-ide -> hydro-...-ic (hydrochloric); -ate -> -ic (sulfuric); -ite -> -ous (sulfurous).
hypochlorite (-ite) -> -ous acid; the hypo- prefix is kept.

HF(aq) = H + one other element, no O -> binary acid; HNO3 and H2SO4 are oxoacids, NaOH is a base.
H2SO4 is an oxoacid from sulfate -> sulfuric acid (hydrosulfuric acid is actually H2S(aq)).
Group 15 -> 5 valence e- (1 pair + 3 single dots); 3 unpaired e- -> bonding capacity 3 (= 8 - 5).
C has 4 valence e- and needs 4 more for an octet -> 4 bonds.
O has 6 valence e-: 2 pairs + 2 singles (N = 1 pair + 3 singles, F = 3 pairs + 1 single, C = 4 singles).
H matches He with 2 valence e- (duet; course note 'H needs 2'). Wording is ambiguous: 'need' could be read as additional electrons (1).
Each K lost its single valence e- (K+ drawn with no dots); S2- gained 2 -> 8 dots, in brackets with 2- charge.
7 valence e-, one unpaired -> one bond completes the octet.
Octet rule: main-group atoms gain, lose, or share e- to reach 8 valence electrons (noble-gas configuration).
Si has bonding capacity 4 like C (CH4) -> four Si-H single bonds.
